attributes.body:
つもりだ (or です) is a grammar point that can have several meanings in Japanese, but is often translated simply as 'intend to (A)', or 'plan to (A)'. It can be used after the plain (dictionary) form of verbs, or after the ない form.

In the last two sentences, there is quite a large difference in nuance, and can be thought of as similar to the difference between 'to intend not to' ないつもり, and 'to have no intention of' つもりはない in English. The former will mean that (A) is being actively avoided, while the latter will indicate that one simply has no plans to (A).

Fun Fact

The literal meaning of つもり comes from the verb 積（つ）もる, which means 'to pile up', or 'to load'. Due to this, つもり is regularly used to describe people that are doing something that is out of character for them, meaning that they have 'piled up' whatever feeling was required to act that way.

In this example, the nuance of つもり is 'so you're really going to act like you're apologizing?!' However, the literal meaning is closer to 'so you've really piled up enough (nerve) in order to act like that's an apology?!'

Caution

The は in つもりはない is interchangeable with が or じゃ (usually では is not used). The difference in nuance is that が gives the impression of being 'uninterested' in (A), while じゃ simply expresses that (A) is not the intended result.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: つもりだ is used to express personal intentions or plans, similar to 'I hope to' or 'I intend to' in English. In contrast, はずだ expresses an expectation or belief that something will happen, based on logic or evidence. While つもりだ is subjective and often refers to the speaker's own plans, はずだ is more objective and is used for expectations about others or events outside the speaker's control.

first_relatable.title: つもりだ
first_relatable.meaning: To plan to, To intend to

attributes.body: つもり basically means 'intention.' When used at the end of a sentence in the form つもりだ, it expresses future plans, similar to 'I intend to' or 'I hope to.' In the form つもりで, it connects to another part of the sentence and means doing something with a certain intention or belief in mind. When preceded by a past tense verb, つもり can also mean 'pretending' or 'acting as if... (though it's not actually the case).'

attributes.body: Both つもりだ and 〜ようと思う・〜おうと思う can both be used to express intentions or plans for the future. つもりだ feels slightly more 'official' or definite, similar to the English 'I intend to' or 'I hope to'. In contrast, 〜ようと思う・〜おうと思う has a more casual and less definitive feel, similar to the English 'I'm thinking of (doing something)'.

attributes.body: Both つもりだ and よていだ express future intentions or plans, but with different nuances. つもりだ emphasizes personal intent or decision, such as 'I intend to' or 'I hope to,' without necessarily implying a set timeframe. よていだ focuses more on planning or scheduling, suggesting that the action is expected to happen at a specific time.
